Let $L = \{m u + n v : m,n\in\mathbb Z\}$ with $u,v$ unit and angle $60°$. For any symmetry $g$, write $g(x)=Ax+t$ with $A\in O(2)$. Since $g(0)=t$ and $0\in L$, $t\in L$, so $g$ is composition of translation by $t$ and linear map $A$. The linear part must satisfy $A(L)=L$. Conversely any such $A$ and $t\in L$ give symmetry. Thus
$$G/(T\cap G) \cong P = \{A\in O(2): A L=L\},$$
where $T\cap G$ is translations by vectors of $L$.

Now $P$ is the point group. It fixes $0$ and acts on the six nearest neighbors of $0$: $\pm u, \pm v, \pm(v-u)$. These form a regular hexagon, so $P$ is a subgroup of $D_6$ (order 12). Conversely, $R$ (rotation by $60°$) and $S$ (reflection in line through $u$) preserve $L$, and generate all 12 symmetries of the hexagon. Hence $|P|=12$.

Therefore
$$[G:T\cap G] = |P| = 12.$$

Let \(L\) be an equilateral triangular lattice. Choose a basis of \(L\) consisting of two unit vectors making a \(60^\circ\) angle, and write

\[
L=\{m\mathbf u+n\mathbf v : m,n\in\mathbb Z\}.
\]

Any Euclidean symmetry of \(L\) is an isometry of the form

\[
x\mapsto Ax+t,
\]

where \(A\in O(2)\). Since \(0\in L\), its image \(t\) must also lie in \(L\). Thus every symmetry is a composition of a translation by a lattice vector with a linear orthogonal map preserving \(L\).

The subgroup \(T\cap G\) consists precisely of the translations by vectors of \(L\):

\[
T\cap G=\{x\mapsto x+\mathbf w:\mathbf w\in L\}.
\]

Therefore the quotient \(G/(T\cap G)\) is the group of orthogonal transformations \(A\) fixing the origin such that \(A(L)=L\), i.e. the point group of the triangular lattice.

Now fix the origin. The six nearest lattice points to the origin are

\[
\pm \mathbf u,\quad \pm \mathbf v,\quad \pm(\mathbf v-\mathbf u),
\]

which form a regular hexagon. Hence the stabilizer of the origin in \(G\) is exactly the symmetry group of a regular hexagon: the six rotations by multiples of \(60^\circ\) and the six reflections. Its order is therefore \(12\).

Thus

\[
[G:T\cap G]=12.
\]

\[
\boxed{12}
\]
